notes: Account summary: mid-stage enterprise adtech platform building a real-time personalization layer using chat + reranking. Strong cost-sensitivity; wants predictable unit economics for peak shopping events.
Primary ask: dedicated capacity with explicit throughput guarantees rather than best-effort reserved GPUs. NeoQuill wants a minimum tokens/sec floor to guarantee tail latency during campaigns.
Throughput specifics requested by customer (from procurement):
- Steady-state minimum: 11,000 tokens/sec across the fleet (observed workload: mix of short chat turns ~25 tokens and longer rerank flows up to 800 tokens).
- Concurrency cap: guarantee 60 concurrent generation sessions with per-session bucket isolation (sessions vary: 0.5-5 qps each).

- Burst policy: allow bursts up to 220 concurrent sessions or 75k tokens/sec for up to 90 seconds to cover flash promotions; bursts beyond that should be auto-throttled to soft-fail and optionally route to hosted fallback models.

- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile generation latency target <= 150ms/token, 99th percentile <= 300ms/token under guaranteed throughput floor. Customer will tolerate degraded latency during bursts if informed by metrics and fallbacks are enforced.

- Reserved GPU planning: prefer fixed instance types (A100 or equivalent), want list of supported quantizations and expected tokens/sec per GPU for their model family. Requesting a sizing worksheet mapping steady-state tokens/sec to number of reserved GPUs and headroom for autoscale/burst.
- Fallbacks & routing: require policy that routes to a cheaper / smaller quantized variant when capacity is exhausted, plus automatic retry/backoff. Must support model pinning for critical flows.
- Monitoring & penalties: want token-level billing visibility, 1-minute resolution latency/throughput metrics, and credits if Redwood fails to meet the min tokens/sec SLA more than 3 times/month.
- Security: VPC peering + customer-managed KMS; strict retention controls for PII; audit log export to their SIEM.
Customer quotes: 'We need to know how many tokens per second we can count on during our campaigns — bursty traffic kills conversion if models slow down.'

SE notes: need to produce a conservative sizing table. Early profiling shows our recommended model (open-llm-family-7b-q8) yields ~2.6k steady tokens/sec per A100-equivalent when using continuous batching and prefix cache. That implies ~5 GPUs sustained for floor but with concurrency isolation requirement may push to 8-10 reserved nodes depending on headroom and redundancy.

Commercial: NeoQuill pushing for explicit concurrency cap language and an express burst window (90s) with clear behavior beyond window (queue vs degrade). Legal also asked for sample indemnity and data residency clauses.
Action items: produce GPU sizing worksheet, draft SLA redline with throughput floor + burst policy, prepare a short demo showing burst handling and fallback routing (drive link).
